metadata.case_name: WONG SUN CHEONG, SUING BY HIS NEXT FRIEND LEE YIN SHEUNG v. CHOI CHI KONG AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: Delivery man at Kai Ming Food Shop; also did part‑time delivery work (soya milk and noodles)

injuries.description: Severe head injury with skull fractures and multiple intracranial haemorrhages and contusion of the brain substance
injuries.body_part: head / brain (left side skull fracture noted)
injuries.source: "Radiological investigations showed fractures on the left side of his skull, subarachnoid bleeding, subdural bleeding as well as contusion of the brain substance."

injuries.description: Post‑traumatic epilepsy (status epilepticus in August 2012; on antiepileptic drug phenytoin)
injuries.source: "In August 2012, while having lunch at home, he developed status epilepticus with refractory generalized epileptic seizures... He was then started on the antiepileptic drug phenytoin which he continues to take."
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

manifestations.description: Prolonged post‑traumatic amnesia (estimated as over one month)
Cognitive dysfunction (MMSE 18/30; mild to moderate dementia)
Naming difficulty; impaired ability to express himself (often using the wrong words) and impaired understanding of verbal communications
Mild spasticity of the right leg with heightened reflexes
Truncal ataxia; unable to walk heel to toe; impaired balance
Seizures / status epilepticus (controlled after August 2012; on phenytoin; seizure‑free since that one occasion)

treatments_received: Emergency operation to evacuate blood clots
Second emergency operation to evacuate more blood clots
Cranioplasty (repair skull defect with metallic prosthesis) in May 2012
Admission to intensive care unit and intubation for status epilepticus

losses.description: "P is not capable of managing his own legal and financial affairs and is not fully independent even inside the home."
"with P’s cognitive dysfunction, dysphasia, incontinence and impaired balance, P was not employable in any capacity. His permanent loss of earning capacity was 100%."
"as a result of the severe head injury P had ... cognitive dysfunction"

"as a result of the severe head injury P had dysphasia (problem with language) ... impaired ability to express himself (often using the wrong words) as well as understanding of verbal communications."
